reading: The grid is cut into panels by full separator lines. One panel holds a shape; the first panel of each panel-row holds a colour block. Every panel in a panel-row gets a copy of the shape in that row's colour, and the colour blocks are replaced by the shape too.
verb: stamp shape into every panel, coloured per row

slots.unit: the one non-square shape found in some panel (its pattern inside the panel)
slots.colour: the colour of the block in the first panel of that panel-row

why: every output panel equals the shape pattern drawn in its row's key colour on background

reading: Panels come in left/right pairs separated by background lines. The shapes swap: each panel keeps its own background colour and shows the other panel's shape, drawn in the other panel's background colour.

slots.pair: the left and right panel on the same rows
slots.subject: the non-background shape cells of each panel
slots.position: same relative position inside the panel

why: out_left = bg(left) except where right has shape -> bg(right); out_right = bg(right) except where left has shape -> bg(left)

reading: One large colour object is a coarse 3x3 pattern made of equal square blocks; it is shrunk to 3x3 (one cell per block) and drawn in the colour of the scattered noise pixels.
verb: downscale largest object, recolour with noise colour

slots.subject: the largest object (blocky pattern of k x k squares)
slots.scale: block size k = object box size / 3

why: output cell (i,j) is the noise colour iff block (i,j) of the large object's box is filled

reading: Key pairs at the left edge map shape colours to new colours. Around each shape, every background cell of its box grown by one cell that is reachable from outside (not an enclosed hole) is painted with key(shape colour).
verb: halo each object in its key colour

slots.key: 2-cell horizontal pairs a,b at the left edge (a -> b)
slots.subject: each object other than the key
slots.region: background cells in the object's bounding box expanded by 1 that are 4-connected to the box edge (enclosed holes excluded)

why: every changed cell is outside-reachable background within one expanded object box and gets key of that object's colour

reading: The output is the input scaled by its own size: every foreground cell of the input becomes a full copy of the input, every background cell an empty block.
why: output block (i,j) is the input if input[i][j] is non-background, else empty

reading: Each 2x2 square shoots a diagonal line of its own colour to the grid border: colour 1 goes up-left from its top-left corner, colour 2 goes down-right from its bottom-right corner.
why: each ray is a diagonal of the object's colour starting next to its corner and ending at the border; direction fixed per colour (1 up-left, 2 down-right)

reading: Three equally spaced pixels lie on a diagonal; the middle one is the centre and their spacing d is the step. Concentric square rings of that colour are drawn around the centre at every Chebyshev distance that is a multiple of d, clipped to the grid.

slots.centre: the middle of the three markers

why: out cell is colour iff max(|y-cy|,|x-cx|) mod d == 0

reading: Two separator columns cut the grid into three equal panels. The output panel is assembled column-wise: left columns from the first panel, the middle column from the second, right columns from the third.

slots.panels: three panels cut by the separator columns
slots.slice: for width 5: cols 0-1 from panel 1, col 2 from panel 2, cols 3-4 from panel 3 (the left/middle/right part of each)

why: every output column equals the same-index column of the panel assigned to that position

reading: A single pixel shoots diagonal lines of its colour in all four diagonal directions until the grid border.
why: every cell on the two diagonals through the marker is its colour; all other cells are background

reading: The single-colour shape is cut into 2x2 squares and L-trominoes; each piece is recoloured by its shape: square -> 1, L missing top-left -> 2, L missing bottom-left -> 3, L missing top-right -> 4.
verb: decompose shape into pieces and colour by piece type

slots.subject: the fg shape
slots.pieces: a tiling of it by 2x2 squares and 3-cell L shapes (2x2 minus one corner)
slots.key: piece type -> colour: full square 1, missing TL 2, missing BL 3, missing TR 4

why: every output fg cell belongs to one piece, colour set by the piece's missing corner
invariants: the set of fg cell positions
